item.title: Tata Sons board meet postponed to Nov 30 after Noel raises concerns
item.description: Tata Sons on Monday postponed a crucial board meeting which was set to discuss the way ahead on the listing of the holding company of the country's largest conglomerate by four days to November 30. The postponement has been necessitated after a letter from Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata on Sunday raising concerns about the mandatory seven-day notice period for a board meeting not being followed, as the agenda was put up only four days in advance. The agenda for the meeting has not been changed, and it is only the day which has been postponed to November 30 from November 26 earlier to give sufficient time for all the directors to prepare for the meeting, as per people in the know. The crucial meeting on November 30 will discuss items including RBI-mandated listing of Tata Sons or ways ahead on complying with the central bank's requests, they said. Divisions among the top echelons on the way ahead for the group had come into the open at the last board meet of Tata Sons on September 1

"We are specifically looking to invest around Rs 3,000 crore in critical minerals facility expansion over the next five years. item.title: MPCB asks Adani firm to stop work on temporary labour camp in Satara
item.description: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) has directed Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd to stop excavation and construction work for its temporary camp in Satara district for allegedly beginning these without obtaining the necessary environmental clearance and permissions. The labour camp in Satara's Patan taluka, some 300 kilometres from here, is part of the firm's 1500 MW Tarali Pumped Storage Project. In a stop-work notice dated November 20, the MPCB said the company had started excavation and development work at Gat Nos. 33 and 34 in Sawargahar village for a temporary labour camp and other storage activities without informing the board or obtaining the required permissions. The company had not secured environmental clearance for the excavation and development work from the competent authority, the MPCB added. The notice, issued under Section 33A of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974, and Section 31A of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act .
item.bs:keywords: Adani Renewable Energy One, Maharashtra Pollution Control Board, MPCB, Tarali Pumped Storage Project, Satara, Patan taluka, environmental clearance, stop-work notice, pumped storage project, environmental regulations, construction permissions, Maharashtra

item.title: ITC extends Braille-enabled packaging to Fiama, takes total to 16 SKUs
item.description: Alongside an industry-wide shift toward AI-enabled personalisation and algorithmic optimisation, diversified conglomerate ITC Ltd is pursuing an analogue, inclusive approach to product innovation by incorporating raised Braille text on select personal care items from its Savlon and Fiama portfolios. The initiative makes everyday consumer products more accessible to millions of visually impaired people in India, for whom routine activities such as identifying a handwash bottle or choosing the right personal care product can pose challenges. Building on Savlon's introduction of India's first Braille-enabled FMCG packaging in 2018, ITC's Personal Care Products Business has now extended the initiative to Fiama. It now has 16 SKUs from the personal care segment under accessible packaging. Braille identifiers are currently featured on technically feasible product packs, such as Savlon Antiseptic Disinfectant Liquid, Savlon Wet Wipes and Handwash Pumps, as well as Fiama Shower Gels. item.title: Airbnb looks beyond traditional holiday hubs to deepen presence in India
item.description: Global hospitality platform Airbnb is looking to deepen its presence in India by expanding beyond traditional holiday destinations, strengthening the homestay ecosystem and bringing more local entrepreneurs onto its platform to tap the country's growing domestic travel market. item.title: EV brand E-Went eyes mass market, to test sodium-ion batteries from Dec
item.description: Kolkata-based Saraogi E-Ventures, which markets electric two-wheelers under the E-Went brand, sees significant growth opportunities in India's price-sensitive markets, particularly in the sub-Rs 1 lakh segment, while exploring sodium-ion battery technology as an alternative to conventional lithium-ion batteries, its founder and CEO Umang Kumar Saraogi said. The company plans to begin trials of sodium-ion battery-powered scooters around December, deploying some vehicles for testing. The technology is being explored for its potential safety advantages over conventional lithium-ion batteries, although its relatively lower energy density makes the battery packs bulkier, Saraogi said. "It is supposed to be safer. We expect to conduct trials here starting in December and deploy some vehicles with these batteries. The economics and convenience have to be evaluated before we can deploy them in our new product launches. Currently, most of the models use lithium-ion technology," he told PTI.
